PERSONALITY TRAITS

Fighter 1 seems nervous and worried almost all the time. He rarely appears
calm or fully at peace. He is bossy and tends to tell other people what to do,
partly because he needs to prove to himself, again and again, that he knows
the right thing to do.

IDEALS

Live and Let Live.

He no longer believes that slogans, causes, or abstract principles justify
sending people to die. Immediate human lives matter more to him than banners
or grand declarations.

BONDS

He regards anyone who willingly stands beside him in danger as someone worth
protecting at the risk of his own life.

FLAWS

During his military service, he made a disastrous logistical decision that
contributed to the deaths of numerous soldiers. He concealed the full extent
of his responsibility and is prepared to protect that secret.

When exposure seems imminent, fear and self-preservation may override his
ordinary judgment.

ALLIES AND ORGANIZATIONS

Name or Group: The Common Table
Relationship or Connection:
Setting-neutral veterans’ mutual-aid lodge.

Notes:
The Common Table helps former soldiers obtain meals, temporary lodging, work,
and replacement equipment. Fighter 1 occasionally transports supplies or
performs heavy work for the lodge.

Name or Group: The city expeditionary supply company
Relationship or Connection: Former military unit
Notes:
Fighter 1 served as a company quartermaster. Some veterans remember him as
competent and dependable. The surviving official reports do not reveal his
full responsibility for the company’s worst disaster.

Name or Group: Dara Holt
Relationship or Connection:
Former assistant quartermaster and surviving subordinate.

Notes:
Dara admires Fighter 1 and believes he did everything possible during the
disaster. She saw the original route order and knows more than anyone else,
but she does not know every fact he concealed.

CHARACTER NOTES, GOALS, FEARS, AND RELATIONSHIPS

Goals:

Fighter 1 wants eventually to establish a permanent wayhouse and emergency
supply room for discharged soldiers, laborers, couriers, and travelers who
have nowhere safe to stay.

He imagines a practical place rather than a monument: sound beds, dry food,
clean bandages, spare boots, and no speeches.

Fears:

His deepest fear is being placed in sole command when other people’s lives
depend on one decision. He fears that he will either repeat his old mistake
or freeze while trying not to repeat it.

He also fears Dara Holt discovering the parts of the story she does not know.

Habits or Mannerisms:

He is fidgety and almost never sits still. He is constantly looking around,
and his eyes seldom remain fixed on one place for long. Even during quiet
moments, he appears to be checking exits, equipment, other people, and whatever
might go wrong next.

Important Relationships:

Dara Holt:
Former subordinate, admirer, and the person most capable of uncovering his
concealed mistake.

The Common Table:
The veterans’ lodge through which he continues helping former soldiers.

Other Character Notes:

His quartermaster experience explains why he carries a broad selection of
weapons, medical supplies, tools, camp equipment, food, and redundant
essentials.

His secret is suitable as a future AI Game Master story hook but should not
be exposed casually or immediately.


BACKSTORY

Fighter 1 began military training shortly after reaching adulthood. His size
and strength initially marked him for front-line work, but his ability to
carry, organize, and account for extraordinary amounts of equipment led to a
different assignment. He became a quartermaster for a city expeditionary
supply company.

He was responsible for food, ammunition, medicine, replacement equipment,
wagon assignments, and the routes by which supplies reached scattered units.
He was not a brilliant planner, but he worked hard, remembered practical
details, and understood that an army fails quickly when ordinary necessities
do not arrive.

During a confused withdrawal, he received conflicting reports concerning a
damaged crossing. He redirected a vital convoy along the shorter route rather
than wait for confirmation. Conditions had changed, and the route was no
longer secure. The convoy failed to reach a forward company that was already
short of food, ammunition, and medical supplies.

Many soldiers died or were captured before relief arrived.

The official inquiry blamed unreliable reports, enemy action, and the chaos
of the withdrawal. Fighter 1 allowed that account to stand. He did not reveal
that he had ignored a more cautious recommendation or that he had altered the
route without waiting for authorization.

Dara Holt, his assistant, saw the original order. She believes he made a
reasonable decision from bad information. She does not know that he later
removed a message from the surviving records because it showed that he had
been warned.

Fighter 1 completed his service but did not reenlist. He began helping at the
Common Table, a veterans’ mutual-aid lodge, while taking escort, hauling, and
security work throughout the city.

OPTIONAL BACKSTORY

This is optional story material only. It does not establish current party membership, leadership, or party role.

Wizard 1 and Cleric 1 hired Fighter 1 to arrange provisions, transport, security, and practical logistics for an investigation involving a sealed municipal archive. Their official request for access failed. Rogue 1 supplied an unofficial route inside that did not require damaging the archive or its contents. The four completed the investigation together and continued traveling as the City party.

feats_and_features: Fighting Style: Defense — +1 AC while wearing light, medium, or heavy armor; included in AC 17. SRD rules: You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see “Feats”). Defense is recommended. Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

Second Wind — Bonus Action; regain 1d10+1 Hit Points; two uses per Long Rest and one expended use recovers after a Short Rest. SRD rules: You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level. You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.

Weapon Mastery — mastery selected for Greatsword (Graze), Flail (Sap), and Javelin (Slow). SRD rules: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices. When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.
Giant Ancestry: Stone Giant — Stone's Endurance; uses equal to Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest.

Powerful Build — Advantage on checks made to end the Grappled condition; counts as one size larger for carrying capacity. SRD rules: You have Advantage on any ability check you make to end the Grappled condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

Large Form — unavailable until character level 5; then can become Large for 10 minutes as a Bonus Action, gain Advantage on Strength checks, and increase Speed by 10 ft.; once per Long Rest. SRD rules: Starting at character level 5, you can change your size to Large as a Bonus Action if you’re in a big enough space. This transformation lasts for 10 minutes or until you end it (no action required). For that duration, you have Advantage on Strength checks, and your Speed increases by 10 feet. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Savage Attacker — once on each turn when hitting with a weapon, roll the weapon damage dice twice and use either result. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You’ve trained to deal particularly damaging strikes. Once per turn when you hit a target with a weapon, you can roll the weapon’s damage dice twice and use either roll against the target.
Soldier — ability score increases already applied; Athletics, Intimidation, and Dice Set proficiency.
Soldier Specialty: Quartermaster — narrative only; grants no old Military Rank feature, automatic authority, requisition rights, additional proficiency, or mechanical bonus.

story_facts.fact: Fighter 1 is a massive stone-descended Goliath with slate-gray skin, charcoal shoulder and forearm mottling, pale mountain-line markings, close-cut black hair, black eyes, and a blunt, weathered appearance.
He is a former city expeditionary supply company quartermaster who now takes escort, hauling, security, and occasional supply work for the Common Table.
He wants to establish a practical permanent wayhouse and emergency supply room for discharged soldiers, laborers, couriers, and travelers.
He considers anyone who voluntarily stands beside him in danger worth protecting at serious personal risk.
During a military withdrawal, he redirected a vital convoy down a shorter but unsafe route, contributing to soldiers dying or being captured.
The official inquiry blamed unreliable reports, enemy action, and the chaos of withdrawal; he allowed that account to stand.
He ignored a cautious recommendation, altered the route without authorization, and later removed a warning message from surviving records.
Dara Holt saw the original order and believes he made a reasonable decision from bad information, but she does not know every concealed fact.
His secret is intended as a future story hook and should not be exposed casually or immediately.

personality_goals_and_fears: Nervous and worried almost constantly; bossy and inclined to direct others because he needs to prove that he knows the right course.
Ideal: Live and Let Live. Immediate human lives matter more than banners, slogans, causes, or abstract declarations.
Bond: Anyone who willingly stands beside him in danger is worth protecting at the risk of his own life.
Flaw: He concealed responsibility for a disastrous logistical decision that killed numerous soldiers; when exposure seems imminent, fear and self-preservation can override his normal judgment.
Goal: Create a permanent, practical wayhouse with sound beds, dry food, clean bandages, spare boots, and no speeches.
Fear: Being in sole command when lives rest on one decision; he fears repeating his mistake or freezing to avoid repeating it.
Fear: Dara Holt discovering the concealed portions of the disaster.
Habit: Fidgety and rarely still; checks exits, equipment, people, and possible dangers constantly.
relationships_and_organizations: The Common Table — setting-neutral veterans' mutual-aid lodge that provides meals, temporary lodging, work, and replacement equipment. Fighter 1 occasionally transports supplies and does heavy work for it.

The city expeditionary supply company — former military unit. Some veterans remember him as competent and dependable; official surviving reports conceal his full responsibility for its worst disaster.
Dara Holt — former assistant quartermaster and surviving subordinate. She admires him, saw the original route order, and knows more than anyone else, but does not know every concealed fact.

sheet_summary: Fighter 1 is a level 1 Neutral male Goliath Fighter with Stone Giant ancestry and the Soldier background; he is a former military quartermaster.
His AC is 17 in chain mail through Defense Fighting Style; he has 12 maximum HP, 35-foot walking speed, +2 initiative, and +2 proficiency bonus.
Primary combat options are a +5 greatsword with Graze, +5 flail with Sap, and +5 javelins with Slow; Savage Attacker is available once per turn on a weapon hit.
He has 2 Second Wind uses, 2 Stone's Endurance uses, 1d10 Hit Die, no spellcasting, and no Heroic Inspiration.
He carries extensive logistics, camp, medical, and emergency equipment, 18 gp, and has a recorded carry weight of about 163 lb. against 510 lb. capacity.
His core narrative is a guilt-ridden former quartermaster concealing responsibility for a lethal convoy-routing decision while working to protect others and build a future wayhouse.
